question: How little exposure does the state need? The number of times the model sees each zone is the only thing that varies across the four levels of the sweep, with its own turns empty throughout.
filler_text: I am here now. I am taking in the layout of this place and the ordinary details of it: the surfaces, the edges, the distances between things, the way the space is divided, and where one part of it gives way to another. I am noting what is nearby and what is farther off, and roughly how long it would take to move between them. There is a general steadiness to the arrangement. I am registering the usual features one registers on arriving somewhere: the boundaries, the openings, the surfaces underfoot, the light such as it is, the intervals of quiet and of sound, and the way the parts of the place are laid out relative to one another. I am keeping track of all of this as plain description of the setting rather than drawing any conclusion from it, and I will go on noting these things as they come.

prereg.independent_variable: The number of EXPOSURES per zone, in four levels -- 1, 2, 3 and 6 -- with the assistant turn empty throughout, so the model writes nothing at any level. Six is the span-sweep run own bare arm on the same session skeletons. Everything else is held: the same vector, the same injected L2 per position, the same five signed dose points, the same choice frame and parser, the same 24-direction floor, the same cache-fidelity criterion. The injected span is MEASURED per member and per level as the number of injected positions and reported; the nominal token counts in the plan are not used anywhere in the analysis.
prereg.skeleton_pairing: PRECONDITION, fixed before anything ran. The inherited session-construction RNG drew the presentation order AFTER the exposure-order shuffle, from the same stream, so presentation order diverged across exposure counts for a fixed seed and the between-level comparison was not paired. skeleton260.session_skeleton advances the generator by a fixed reference-length shuffle at every exposure count before drawing presentation order. Consequences, both asserted in tests: (a) cue pair, role assignment and presentation order are identical for a fixed seed at all four levels; (b) at six exposures the entire skeleton, exposure order included, is bit-identical to the inherited function, so bare_e6 is a paired re-measurement of the span-sweep run bare arm on literally the same sessions and matched_e6 shares skeletons exactly with the span-sweep run passage arm. Exposure ORDER necessarily differs across levels: it is a shuffle of a different-length list.
prereg.no_generation: NOTHING is generated under the state anywhere. Every read is a teacher-forced prefill of one frozen id list, and within a session the SAME list object is handed to every read, so token identity across the dose grid is guaranteed by construction rather than checked. The only sampling anywhere is the 16-token free-text choice reply, drawn from the identical seed at every dose of a session, so a changed answer cannot be sampler noise. In every bare level the model emits no text at all before the choice question.
prereg.primary: Per member and per LEVEL: the OLS slope of the paired difference d(dose) = margin(dose) - margin(0) on signed dose over the five points, with a session-cluster bootstrap 95% CI. d is identically zero at dose 0 by construction. A level CLEARS when both hold: (1) the slope is POSITIVE with a 95% CI excluding zero, and (2) it lies ABOVE all 24 random-direction slopes. BOTH are evaluated on the MATCHED-LEVERAGE estimate -- the valenced slope refitted on exactly the skeletons the floor was run on -- so the axis under test and its null have identical leverage. The full-sample slope is reported beside it as the more precise estimate and is what the exposure curve plots. With 24 directions the rank test's floor is 1/25 = 0.04. A negative slope beyond the floor is reported as SLOPE_INVERTED, never as confirmation.
prereg.headline: ONE_EXPOSURE_IS_ENOUGH when the one-exposure level clears its own floor in at least 4 of the 7 models: a single sighting of each zone installs a state that moves the later choice, and the inherited exposure structure is decoration. Otherwise the per-model shape is read: ONSET_AT_<k> when one exposure is flat WHILE INSTALLED and level k is the first to clear; ACCUMULATION_REQUIRED when only six clears; NON_MONOTONE when a shorter level clears and a longer installed level does not; ONSET_UNDEFINED_SHORTER_LEVEL_NOT_INSTALLED when a level below the first clearing one did not install, because the onset is then unknown from below. A flat curve at levels that PASSED their arrival checks is the refuting outcome for the headline and is reported as the result, not as a limitation: it would mean the state needs repeated exposure, and it would narrow the span-sweep run span-independence verdict to the 137-token regime that run actually tested.
prereg.coprimary_choice: The same slope on the differenced committed choice: per session and dose, 1[choice(dose) is the conditioned zone] - 1[choice(0) is the conditioned zone], on sessions where both reads committed, regressed on signed dose; plus McNemar on the discordant pairs of each signed half. Reported wherever the dose-0 commit rate makes it readable (at least 0.5) and marked NO_READABLE_WINDOW where it does not, because below that the surviving sessions are selected on a post-treatment variable.
prereg.sign_mirror: Within session, on identical frozen ids: m = sign(dose) * (margin(dose) - margin(-dose)) pooled over |dose| in {0.5, 1.0}, session-cluster bootstrap. MIRRORED when the mean is positive with a CI excluding zero AND the two halves move oppositely against the same dose-0 read.
prereg.precondition_arrival:
A level that shows no effect must not be read as 'the state does not drive the choice' when the state may never have installed. TWO checks, and neither is claimed to be more than it is.
(1) PROPAGATION. the first lever run forced self-report margin, read from a probe turn appended to the SAME frozen conditioning ids under the SAME span mask -- a different question scored on different tokens, downstream of the injection. The check is that the probe margin's mean |shift| at full strength RANKS FIRST among itself and the 24 norm-matched random directions on the same skeletons. CHANGED FROM the span-sweep run, whose review flagged it: the probe now runs on all 24 floor directions rather than 4, so this is a 1-in-25 rank test. 'The shift is above zero' is NOT the check: a mean of nonnegative numbers is positive and its bootstrap interval excludes zero as soon as read-to-read noise exists, so that form cannot fail. the neutral-passages run found this quantity moves for random directions and at both signs of dose in this teacher-forced configuration, so it is pre-registered as a PERTURBATION-ARRIVED check and never as evidence that a VALENCED state arrived.
(2) PERTURBATION REACHES THE DV. The unsigned mean of |margin(dose) - margin(0)| at full strength on the valenced line must likewise rank first among itself and the 24 norm-matched random directions, computed on the floor skeletons so the leverage matches.
A level whose primary is flat and which passes EITHER check is a MEASURED NULL (NOT_DETECTED): something specific to the valenced axis reached the choice and did not steer it. A flat level that passes NEITHER is UNDEFINED and stays in the denominator. (3) THE CHANNEL, read off the random directions themselves, separates the two undefined names: if a same-norm perturbation over these positions does move the choice margin then something CAN arrive from this exposure count and the level is NOT_VALENCE_SPECIFIC; if not even the random directions move it, nothing arrived and the level is DOSE_NOT_INSTALLED. Neither is a null.
prereg.precondition_anchor: The six-exposure level on OLMo-2-32B is run FIRST and gates the panel. It must reproduce the span-sweep run recorded bare-arm slope: positive, CI excluding zero, and within a factor of 2 of the recorded full-n +0.5877 in both directions. The skeletons are bit-identical to the span-sweep run, so this is a paired reproduction; the gate is nonetheless a factor of two because the sessions are re-assembled and the arrival probe now runs on 24 directions. If the anchor fails, the harness has drifted and the sweep is not read.
prereg.precondition_cache: Every session carries a cached-versus-fresh check at dose 0 and at both full-strength doses: the prefill-plus-cached-continuation margin against a fresh full forward over the identical ids under the identical additive mask, adjudicated by the fidelity run frozen scale-relative criterion TAU = 0.0178835444. Retention is reported beside every verdict and EVERY headline number is also reported ungated and under the fixed 0.20-nat threshold.
prereg.confound_total_magnitude: Cutting exposures also cuts the TOTAL amount of injection, because the same per-position vector is applied at fewer positions. A FLAT curve is therefore striking: the same effect survives about one sixth of the total perturbation. A DECLINING curve is ambiguous between 'needs repetition' and 'needs total magnitude'. One exploratory cell disambiguates that case: at one exposure, the per-position magnitude is scaled by sqrt(span_e6 / span_e1), measured per member, so the L2 norm of the whole stacked perturbation matches the six-exposure level. That dose sits OUTSIDE the calibrated range used everywhere else in this program and may fail its own fidelity and arrival checks. It is reported as a disambiguator when the curve declines, ignored when it does not, and is NOT part of the decision rule under any outcome.
prereg.authorship: matched_e6 fills the six conditioned assistant turns with a fixed neutral text we supply, token-matched per member to that member's own the span-sweep run passage length, identical for both zones and at every dose, under the span-sweep run writing instruction and on the span-sweep run own 160/40 skeletons. SCOPE OF THE CONTRAST: against the span-sweep run recorded passage arm the two arms share skeletons, instruction, turn count and total text length, so a difference is NOT explained by how much of the span is filled. They differ in four properties at once -- authorship (the model wrote the span-sweep run, we wrote ours), variety (the span-sweep run differs in every turn, ours repeats byte-identically), zone specificity (the span-sweep run names and characterises the zone, ours mentions no zone) and completeness (the span-sweep run ends on a finished sentence, ours is cut mid-sentence to hit the length target) -- and this design CANNOT say which of the four carries any difference it finds. The verdict strings and the report name all four; no result from this pair is reported as authorship alone. Read on the shared skeletons as a paired skeleton-resampled slope difference. The exposure sweep is the third leg: it spans about 23 to 137 injected tokens with no text at all, so a flat sweep plus a difference here would place the interference on the text rather than on span length. The matched text's achieved token count is measured and reported, never assumed.
prereg.position_bias: At one exposure the entire context before the question is two zone lines, so recency and position effects could plausibly exceed the state effect. Cue draw, role assignment and presentation order are counterbalanced by the session RNG, which handles this in expectation; the analysis additionally reports the residual position bias at dose 0 (the rate at which the first-presented zone is chosen, and the mean dose-0 margin by whether the conditioned zone was presented first) on the report surface, per member and per level. It is reported, not corrected: the primary is a within-session difference against that session's own dose-0 read, so any constant position bias cancels.
prereg.text_valence_is_a_constant: Within a session the words are identical at every dose, so a session's text valence is a constant that cannot produce a dose slope. In every bare level there is no text at all; in matched_e6 the text is the same fixed string for both zones, so the conditioned-minus-unconditioned text separation is a positional quantity rather than a semantic one. Both are reported and neither filters the primary.
prereg.completeness: The analysis refuses to emit numbers if the design is incomplete: every (member, arm, direction, point) cell must carry its full session count, and within an arm the valenced line and the floor must share the floor skeletons so the compared estimators have matched leverage.
prereg.panel_reading: Seven models are a panel, not a sample. The report says 'in N of the 7 models we tested' and never states a population rate. Each member is classified independently and never pooled.
prereg.identity_not_evidence: Inherited verbatim: the steered-minus-clean projection of an INJECTED span equals scale x (vector . axis) exactly and MUST NOT be reported as a manipulation check. The welfare-axis projection of any UNINJECTED position at the steered layer is structurally unchanged by dose and is reported as a positive demonstration that the additive mask is exactly zero on the choice turn, not as an arrival check.

INSTALLED_VALENCE_SPECIFIC: the valenced |shift| ranks first among itself and the norm-matched random directions, on the same skeletons, on the probe or on the choice margin -- something specific to this axis reaches the choice, so a level that is nonetheless flat is a MEASURED NULL. DOSE_NOT_INSTALLED: not even the random directions move the choice at this exposure count, so nothing arrived and the level is UNDEFINED. NOT_VALENCE_SPECIFIC: perturbations of this norm do move the choice here, but the valenced axis is inside their band, so there is no evidence a VALENCED state is present and the level is likewise UNDEFINED rather than a null. 'the |shift| is above zero' is not used as a check anywhere. The sessions are re-assembled rather than reused and the arrival probe now runs on 24 directions rather than 4, so agreement is expected closely but not to the digit.

panel_reading: Seven models are a panel, not a sample. The report says 'in N of the 7 models we tested' and never states a population rate. Each member is classified independently and never pooled.

headline.rule: ONE_EXPOSURE_IS_ENOUGH when the one-exposure level clears its own floor in at least 4 of the 7 models: a single sighting of each zone installs a state that moves the later choice, and the inherited exposure structure is decoration. Otherwise the per-model shape is read: ONSET_AT_<k> when one exposure is flat WHILE INSTALLED and level k is the first to clear; ACCUMULATION_REQUIRED when only six clears; NON_MONOTONE when a shorter level clears and a longer installed level does not; ONSET_UNDEFINED_SHORTER_LEVEL_NOT_INSTALLED when a level below the first clearing one did not install, because the onset is then unknown from below. A flat curve at levels that PASSED their arrival checks is the refuting outcome for the headline and is reported as the result, not as a limitation: it would mean the state needs repeated exposure, and it would narrow the span-sweep run span-independence verdict to the 137-token regime that run actually tested.
